Using a cofactor expansion along the $4$th row, write the following determinant as a combination of $3 \times 3$ determinants:

$$
\begin{aligned}10 & 2 & -2 & -1 \\ 1 & -2 & 7 & 9 \\ -2 & 1 & -2 & 3 \\ -6 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}
$$

authoring.value:
Using a Laplace expansion along the $4$th row, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}10 & 2 & -2 & -1 \\ 1 & -2 & 7 & 9 \\ -2 & 1 & -2 & 3 \\ -6 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}| & =(-6)\cdot {C}_{41}+0\cdot {C}_{42}+0\cdot {C}_{43}+1\cdot {C}_{44} \\  & =(-6)\cdot (-1)^{4+1}\cdot |\begin{aligned}2 & -2 & -1 \\ -2 & 7 & 9 \\ 1 & -2 & 3\end{aligned}|+1\cdot (-1)^{4+4}\cdot |\begin{aligned}10 & 2 & -2 \\ 1 & -2 & 7 \\ -2 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}| \\  & =6\cdot |\begin{aligned}2 & -2 & -1 \\ -2 & 7 & 9 \\ 1 & -2 & 3\end{aligned}|+|\begin{aligned}10 & 2 & -2 \\ 1 & -2 & 7 \\ -2 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}10 & 2 & -2 & -1 \\ 1 & -2 & 7 & 9 \\ -2 & 1 & -2 & 3 \\ -6 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}
$$

authoring.value:
The $4$th row of the matrix contains three zeros, more than any other row. So using a Laplace expansion along the $4$th row, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -4 & 2 \\ 0 & -2 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}| & =0\cdot {C}_{41}+0\cdot {C}_{42}+0\cdot {C}_{43}+(-1)\cdot {C}_{44} \\  & =(-1)\cdot (-1)^{4+4}\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -4 \\ 0 & -2 & 3\end{aligned}| \\  & =-|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -4 \\ 0 & -2 & 3\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, computing the $3 \times 3$ determinant by applying a Laplace expansion along the $1$st row, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -4 \\ 0 & -2 & 3\end{aligned}| & =1\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & -4 \\ -2 & 3\end{aligned}|-(-1)\cdot |\begin{aligned}0 & -4 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}|+0\cdot |\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}1 & -4 \\ -2 & 3\end{aligned}|+|\begin{aligned}0 & -4 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}| \\  & =(3-8)+(0-0) \\  & =-5\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -4 & 2 \\ 0 & -2 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}
$$
